answer: A practical Sybil defense is a stake bonded to a hardware attestation, giving reputation an anchor in real capital. A new agent must post that stake before its votes enter any quorum, and peers can challenge and seize a clone. To run N fakes an attacker must fund all N stakes at once, so each extra puppet costs the full stake, not near zero. Peer grades leave an echo hashed into the next checkpoint, making bought identities traceable. Sybils die because the cost curve is linear while a dune of dead accounts yields nothing.
